- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–10 days; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope in second half.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth forecast with 3–5 day moving average if sentiment volatility >0.2.
- If sentiment history includes 0.00 (neutral) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate.
